sendAddGuestsEmails called with original guests array instead of filtered uniqueGuests array, causing email logic to misidentify which attendees are new guests
New guests inherit organizer's timezone and locale without consent, causing calendar invites and emails to be formatted for wrong timezone and language

IDOR / Broken Access Control: Booking lookup fetches by id alone without scoping to authenticated user's ownership or organization, allowing attackers to enumerate booking IDs and probe for existence of bookings they don't own

Broken Authorization Logic: Uses AND (&&) instead of OR (||) for team admin/owner check, requiring user to be BOTH team admin AND team owner, effectively disabling the team admin/owner authorization path
When booking.eventType?.teamId is null/undefined, it falls back to 0, causing isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to behave unexpectedly for non-existent team ID
Attendee can add guests to any booking they attend without organizer approval, allowing malicious attendees to add unauthorized guests
Blacklist bypass via case sensitivity: blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest email is compared without lowercasing, allowing bypass with mixed case emails
Frontend error handler displays raw error messages to users, creating latent risk if error messages are modified to include guest emails or other PII
No rate limiting on guest addition endpoint, allowing attackers to add large numbers of guests or trigger email spam to arbitrary addresses
New attendee records are created with empty string name field, creating permanent low-quality data that affects calendar integrations, email templates, and reports that display attendee names
No transaction wrapping database write and calendar update - if updateCalendarAttendees fails after database write, booking record and calendar event become out of sync with no compensation logic
Email sending failures are silently logged with console.log, providing no operator visibility into partial failures while still returning success to users

No server-side validation of booking status before adding guests - guests can be added to cancelled, completed, or rejected bookings, creating orphaned attendee records and triggering emails for events that won't happen

Calendar update failure (updateCalendarAttendees) has no error handling - if calendar provider rejects the update, database is already mutated but calendar is not updated, leaving system in inconsistent state
Email failures in sendAddGuestsEmails are silently swallowed with only console.log, API returns success even when guests never receive notification emails
Promise.all in sendAddGuestsEmails rejects on first failure and drops remaining emails - one bad email address can cause all notifications to fail silently
No timeout on calendar update operation (updateCalendarAttendees) - if calendar provider hangs, request hangs indefinitely consuming server resources
No in-flight guard on Add button allows double-click to trigger duplicate mutation requests, causing confusing success and error toasts
findFirstOrThrow for organizer returns raw 500 error instead of proper 404 when booking.userId is null or user was deleted
Authorization logic uses AND (&&) instead of OR for isTeamAdminOrOwner check, incorrectly requiring users to be BOTH admin AND owner instead of either
